description:
From: Elixir Parity (user-approved 2026-11-24).

Evidence: none of BadFunctionError, BadArityError or SystemLimitError exists as a module in lib/, and nothing in lib/, src/ or runtime/ raises them. So :badfun, {:badarity, _} and :system_limit normalize to ErlangError, where Elixir raises the named exceptions.

Scope: for each of the three, a defexception, a normalize clause, a __reason__ clause, and the runtime raise site.

Related: fz-sc8.169 (apply/2) says its arity mismatch should raise BadArityError, so its clause depends on this ticket.

Done when: an oracle fixture raises and rescues each exception (bad function call, wrong arity, system limit) and matches Elixir on interp, run and build, including the message and the fields.

comments.text: More evidence (Elixir Parity, 2026-11-25): calling a closure with the wrong number of arguments crashes at run time with exit 138, where Elixir raises BadArityError. Example: a closure literal of the wrong arity passed to a spec'd 3-arity callback. Repro: fz-otp-json/probes/mue73/p1.fz. The runtime raise site in this ticket's scope must cover this case.

title: BadFunctionError, BadArityError and SystemLimitError exist, and the runtime raises them as in Elixir
